newsitem.title: GERMANY: West German inflation eases to 1.4 pct in November.
newsitem.headline: West German inflation eases to 1.4 pct in November.

text.p: West German inflation eased to an annual rate of 1.4 percent in November from 1.5 percent in October, continuing a trend of low price pressures in Europe's largest economy, according to figures released Monday.
The Federal Statistics Office said provisional November cost of living data showed prices eased by 0.1 percent in the month from October. Final figures will be released next month.
Economists, who generally see little inflation danger on the horizon in Germany, said the figure reinforced the view that price pressures were likely to remain weak next year.
Commenting on the November data, Trinkaus Capital Management said the fall in the headline rate was "remarkable because of a sharp increase of import prices during the last months."
Each of the four German states whose data make up preliminary west German consumer price data had earlier reported moderate increases in inflation during November.
